title: Cyberbullying Detection with Fairness Constraints
benchmark_measurement: Bias in hate speech detection related to religious identity groups, specifically measuring whether models unfairly classify non-toxic text containing religious identity terms as hate speech.
findings: The proposed fairness-constrained training method significantly reduced bias related to religion in the Gab hate speech dataset. Specifically, it lowered the high false positive rates for the religion and race identity groups, which were the main contributors to bias in the baseline model. This reduction in bias (a 27.5% decrease for the Gab dataset) was achieved while also improving the classification performance (Matthews Correlation Coefficient) for the religion-specific group.
references: S. Hinduja and J. W. Patchin, "Bullying, cyberbullying, and suicide," Archives of Suicide Research, vol. 14, no. 3, pp. 206-221, 2010.
